title: Termwise products of K-injective complexes on a ringed space

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $T$ be a set, and for each $t\in T$ let $I_t^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Assume that the product $I^n=\prod_{t\in T}I_t^n$ exists in $\mathcal A$ for every integer $n$ [def-weil-category-product]. Then the termwise product complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product of the objects $I_t^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-category-product].

proof.text: For a map from an acyclic complex K into the termwise product P, each composite with a projection to I_t admits a null-homotopy by K-injectivity [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Assemble their degree-(p,q) components using the limit in degree q. The homotopy zero and commutation identities hold after every projection, so degreewise limit extensionality proves them. This gives a null-homotopy of the original map, hence P is K-injective. The Lean helper productHomotopy proves the more general assertion for homotopies between any two maps.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of K-injectivity

proof.text: Mathlib isLimitConeOfHasLimitEval gives the termwise cone its limit property in complexes. Lift a cone in the homotopy category componentwise through the full quotient functor and then apply this limit property. The projection equations follow by functoriality. For uniqueness, represent a candidate by a chain map and turn equality of its projections in the homotopy category into component homotopies; productHomotopy assembles them, proving equality in the quotient.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of the product universal property

proof.text: Use the K-injective Hom comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for P and every I_t. The private mapProduct helper transfers a discrete limit through an essentially surjective functor whose maps on morphisms into the cone point and every diagram object are bijective: pull back each cone through an object preimage and the Hom bijections, lift with the original limit, and prove uniqueness using the same bijections. Apply it to Qh and the homotopy-category product of Step 2. Finally transport the limiting cone along quotientCompQhIso, obtaining exactly Q.mapCone P and thus the product [def-weil-category-product].

lean.statement: theorem termwise_product_isKInjective_and_isLimit {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] {T : Type t} (I : T → CochainComplex C ℤ) [∀ s : T, (I s).IsKInjective] [∀ n : ℤ, HasLimit (Discrete.functor I ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)] : let P := HomologicalComplex.coneOfHasLimitEval (Discrete.functor I) IsKInjective P.pt ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone P))
